lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: deriving the ellipse from the sum of focal distances

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: Do an oblique and a right cylinder with the same base and height have equal volume?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 5 and centre O. A point P lies 13 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 8.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 5; the tangent length is 12.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 12.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 12.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 26. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 6. Write its equation.
Compare a sphere of radius r and a cylinder of radius r and height 2r with two cones removed. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3 and centre O. A point P lies 5 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 2.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 4.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 4.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 3; the tangent length is 4.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±3, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±10, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 12. Write its equation.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
